# git-qa

> Open-source human-in-the-loop QA runner. An AI agent works through a test sheet on Android, iPhone, web and desktop apps; a person watches the live screen and signs off each case with one key, and the evidence records who verified what. AI agents can drive it over MCP.

git-qa does not let an AI declare "everything passed". The AI operates the device, browser or desktop app and can only mark a case `AUTO_PASS` (nobody looked). A case becomes `VERIFIED` only when a person presses the key, and their handle goes into the evidence (`run.json` plus the screen at that moment).

## Key facts

- Test sheets are TSV files you can write in any spreadsheet. git-qa never writes back to the sheet.
- Targets: Android devices and emulators (adb), web pages (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, driven over CDP), desktop apps on macOS and Windows, iPhone / iPad (USB mirroring; tapping needs WebDriverAgent on the device).
- The person watches a live view, not a recording. They only look at three things: cases the AI could not judge, cases that changed since last time, and failures. Everything else stays `AUTO_PASS`.
- Evidence goes to `runs/<timestamp>/`: `run.json` (verdicts, steps, who signed off and when) plus a screenshot and optional video per case. No machine-specific paths or personal names, so the folder can live in a public git repository.
- Unattended runs (`--no-ui`) for overnight checks; a person reviews failures later. Stop and resume the next day without re-judging.
- MCP tools: `element_list`, `element_tap`, `device_screen_text`, `device_screenshot`, `device_tap`, `device_swipe`, `device_key`, `device_type`, `device_launch`. There is deliberately no tool that places a verdict.
- Requires Node.js 22 or later. Installers: macOS (one universal build for Apple Silicon and Intel, signed and notarized) and Windows (x64 and ARM64, not signed). Free, MIT license. Status: beta.
- Nothing leaves the machine: the target's screen and the evidence stay on the PC.
